hook_text: A bicycle pedal, a well handle and a pencil sharpener are all the same thing: a wheelbarrow that never stops.
clip_script: Here is a crank: an arm on an axle with a handle at the end. Push the handle round, the axle turns. Pedals, well winders, pencil sharpeners, fishing reels. Now freeze it. The axle is the pivot. The handle, far out, is where you push. The load is the string on the drum, right next to the axle. Load between pivot and effort: that is a second-class lever, same as a wheelbarrow, just bent into a circle so it keeps going. Longer handle, easier turn. Handle over drum is your advantage: 90 over 15 is six, so 60 grams of load needs 10 grams of push. For the crane: a 60 to 90 millimetre handle, a cotton-reel drum, fixed at right angles, and a peg so the load cannot run back down.
visual_style: Whiteboard crank arm with pivot, load and effort marked; a wheelbarrow morphing into a circle; a spring balance reading falling as the handle lengthens.
mood: Playful and sure, one reveal at a time.
pacing: Crank, freeze, label, class, ratio, crane, each a beat or two.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build the crank for your own crane.
